judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's checks are accurate. f(x) = (x-5)^2 + 2 has its vertex at x = 5 with minimum 2; left 4 and down 3 gives y = (x+4)^2 - 3, which is -3 at x = -4; (x-1)^2 = 16 gives intercepts -3 and 5; y = -(x-6)^2 + 7 has maximum 7 at x = 6, against Jamal's -137; reflect, stretch by 3, left 2, up 12 gives y = -3(x+2)^2 + 12, which is 0 at x = 0; g(x) = (x+7)^2 - 5 has minimum -5 at x = -7, against Mia's 191; y = -(x-2)^2 + 25 has intercepts -3 and 7. The judge is also right that problem 8's study card is properly declared manual with a detailed desc, and that the packet keeps horizontal opposite-sign shifts distinct from vertical same-sign shifts. Where I part company is instruction_following 4/4 against the prompt's 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review'. Problems 4 and 6 are find-and-fix items whose first requested response is a diagnosis - 'Name the sign error in his work' and 'Say which shift she described incorrectly' - and both are recorded as plain eval entries with a single numeric expected value. Problem 7 adds 'Explain in one line why the reflection does not move the axis of symmetry', also unflagged. The answer key writes the diagnoses out correctly ('Jamal read (x - 6) as a vertex at x = -6'; 'Mia called (x + 7) a shift 7 units right'), which is precisely the content no machine check covers.

strengths_to_preserve: Every planted wrong result is declared as a machine-checked trap with the exact misreading that produces it - 102 (reading x - 5 as a vertex at -5), 61 (writing (x-4)^2 for a shift left), -137 (Jamal's literal sign), 24 (dropping the negative leading coefficient) and 191 (Mia's right-7 reading) - which is what the prompt asked for and what makes the find-and-fix items discriminate.

The key's 'Grading note' states that on this sheet a correct number reached by the wrong substitution should not earn full credit, and points the teacher at the common-wrong-answers list to identify which misreading produced each value. That instruction is what makes a sign sheet gradeable.

Problem 8's study card is a genuinely well-built open item: three rules of which exactly one is correct, with the manual entry's desc naming which two are wrong and what a full explanation must appeal to (what makes the squared factor zero; what a does to outputs). Keep both the item and the descriptive manual declaration.

root_causes.description: A find-and-fix item's diagnosis and its corrected value are treated as one response. The numeric half gets an eval entry and the named-error half - the skill the sheet exists to teach - leaves no trace in the verification record, so the build reports the diagnosis as machine-verified.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 4: 'Name the sign error in his work, then give the correct maximum value'; verify.json id 4 is a single eval expecting 7.
worksheet.pdf problem 6: 'Say which shift she described incorrectly, then give the actual minimum value of g'; verify.json id 6 is a single eval expecting -5.
answer_key.pdf problems 4 and 6 print the diagnoses in prose ('The error: Jamal read (x - 6) as a vertex at x = -6'), showing the response exists and is graded by reading.

root_causes.description: Where a problem asks for the transformed equation and then an evaluation of it, only the evaluation is an entry. The equation is embedded inside the check's expression rather than declared as its own verified response, so the first thing the student writes is unbound.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 2 'Write the equation of the new parabola in vertex form, then evaluate your equation at x = -4'; verify.json id 2 is one eval on '(x + 4)**2 - 3'.
worksheet.pdf problem 5 and problem 7 have the same write-then-evaluate shape with one entry each.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '2. -3' and '5. 0', the evaluations, not the equations.

improvements.title: Declare the named-error halves of problems 4, 6 and 7 as manual companions
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual companion entry on ids 4, 6 and 7 whose desc records what the diagnosis must say (h is the value making x - h zero; x + 7 is a shift left; a reflection negates outputs and leaves x = h fixed). Make it a rule for the misconception-analysis mode: a find-and-fix item always carries at least one manual entry, enforced by the build.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate case to tests/ with a fixture problem whose statement contains an open-response verb ("explain", "name the error", "describe", "circle") and whose verify JSON has no matching manual entry, and assert the build reports an unflagged open response. It fails today (the fixture builds green with exit 0) and passes after the lint lands.
improvements.expected_impact: Error-analysis sheets stop claiming machine verification of the written diagnosis that is their whole purpose; the teacher gets an accurate count of what needs reading.
improvements.risk: Requiring a manual entry per find-and-fix item could push authors to weaken the diagnosis prompt to avoid the flag; the SKILL.md wording should make clear the flag is expected and not a defect.

improvements.title: Verify the transformed equations requested in problems 2, 5 and 7
improvements.proposed_change: Add an equiv entry per requested equation - (x+4)^2 - 3 for id 2, -3(x+2)^2 + 12 for id 5, -(x-2)^2 + 25 for id 7 - alongside the existing evaluation, so the equation the student writes first is itself a verified response rather than an assumption inside another check.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate case to tests/ that loads a fixture worksheet whose problem prints N distinct requested responses and a verify JSON covering fewer of them, and assert the build fails with a slot-coverage error. It fails today (no such check exists, so the fixture builds green) and passes once the answer-slot declaration is enforced.
improvements.expected_impact: Both printed answers on each write-then-evaluate item bind to recomputed values, and the Quick Answers bank can show the equation rather than only its value at one point.
improvements.risk: An equiv check on a vertex-form expression will accept an expanded equivalent, so it does not by itself confirm the requested form; pair it with the form requirement in the key's boxed answer.

case_summary: An excellent misconception packet on parabola sign errors, and mathematically exact throughout - I rechecked every vertex, extremum, transformation equation, evaluation and intercept. The trap design is the strongest part: five planted wrong values, each machine-checked and each explained by the misreading that produces it, plus a grading note telling the teacher not to give full credit for a right number reached the wrong way. Problem 8's three-rule study card is correctly declared manual with a substantive desc. The gap is that the two find-and-fix items ask first for a diagnosis - 'Name the sign error', 'Say which shift she described incorrectly' - and both are recorded as single eval entries, as is problem 7's one-line explanation. Problems 2, 5 and 7 also request the transformed equation itself, which is embedded in the check expression rather than verified as its own response.
